_core_ebitda_note: BUG FOUND & FIXED (2026-07-30): without this override, generate_dcf.py computes core_ebitda = latest_oi + latest_dep using EDINET's own parsed 'depreciation' field BEFORE overrides are applied. EDINET's D&A extraction returned N/A for 285A (all years), so latest_dep silently defaulted to 0, leaving core_ebitda = 870,369 (== operating income only, not EBITDA). The null-guard at generate_dcf.py L695-701 only fires when core_ebitda is explicitly None, so a merely-wrong non-null auto value was never corrected. This value (1,183,195 = hist_operating_income[-1] 870,369 + hist_depreciation[-1] 312,826, matching the comps CSV self-row EBITDA) feeds Comps Analysis!C21/C27 (Implied Valuation section) which is otherwise silently wrong.

_beta_note: CONFIRMED. validator ALLOWED_KEYS types beta as _NUM only (str '__CONFIRM__' is rejected, unlike current_price/shares_outstanding/net_debt which are _STR_OR_NUM) -- schema code does not support a literal CONFIRM placeholder here, deviating from the prompt's assumption. Value = prompt's own recommended initial value within the specified 1.4-1.7 range. Research check: raw MU beta (2.1-3.3 depending on source) and SNDK beta (3.9-5.4, source-dispersed/unusable) are both inflated by the current AI-memory-cycle volatility, supporting a moderated 1.4-1.7 rather than raw peer readings.
_cost_of_debt_note: CONFIRMED. Pre-tax blended estimate 3.2% x (1-0.30) = 2.24%. Basis: FY2026/3 annual report Note 25 shows total finance costs JPY96,708mn = lease interest 5,823 + interest on amortized-cost financial liabilities 65,570 (bonds+loans+preferred shares combined, not separately broken out) + other 773 + FX-forward derivative losses 24,542. Note 20 confirms preferred shares (redeemed JPY322,996mn, 4/1-7/25/2025 only) are IFRS financial liabilities whose 7.05-9.65% dividend sits inside the 65,570 line. Backing out an estimated preferred-share interest (~7-8bn over the 116-day stub) leaves pure bond+loan interest / average bonds+loans (777,706+1,047,568)/2=912,637 implying pre-tax cost ~6.3% -- still elevated because the new USD bonds carry 6.25%/6.625% coupons. Note 14 discloses these are swapped via cross-currency swaps to JPY-equivalent 3.29%/3.66%, but swap gains sit in OCI (not netted against P&L interest), so the raw ratio overstates true funding cost. Used blended pre-tax 3.2% (swap-adjusted USD bonds ~3.3-3.7% blended with an assumed lower JPY bank-loan rate ~1.5-2.5%). Materiality note: D/(D+E) is only ~3.5% (de_ratio 0.036), so WACC sensitivity to this input is small regardless of the exact figure chosen.

investment_thesis: 1. Cycle position is the entire investment question — FY2026/3 operating margin of 37.2% is not sustainable. The stock trades at 19.1x peak EBITDA against a 4-6x mid-cycle norm, implying the market either expects structural change or has priced in a very different normalization path than a standard DCF.
2. Potential AI-driven structural shift — enterprise SSD demand for AI datacenters may flatten the traditional smartphone/PC-led NAND cycle. If durable, mid-cycle margins reset materially higher.

3. Balance sheet materially repaired — preferred shares fully redeemed (322,996), cash of 470,707, equity attributable to owners nearly doubled to 1,398,929 from 737,565, net debt down to 782,482 from 831,589.
key_risks: 1. Extreme cyclicality — operating profit swung from △252,698 (FY2024/3) to +870,369 (FY2026/3), a 1,123,067 range in three years. Applying any multiple to peak earnings is hazardous.
2. Chinese supply expansion — CXMT/YMTC 3D NAND ramp could impose structural price deflation independent of the demand cycle.

3. Working capital deterioration plus non-deferrable capex — receivables rose 2.77x (238,594 to 660,559) against 1.37x revenue growth; DSO doubled from 51 to 103 days. Capex at 12-14% of revenue cannot pause during a downturn without ceding technology generations.
